generic_sampling_rules.integer_pk: Sequential integers from a fresh base; parent tables' keys are generated first; unique per table; never NULL. For coded-pool PKs (Survey.SurveyID) draw from the coded pool {2013..2020} and skip only keys already present in the compact copy; rows_skipped must be 0 and the generated count must equal table_sizes_per_instance.
generic_sampling_rules.integer_fk: Copy from the parent key pool generated in this instance; if the column is nullable, plant NULL for a small share of rows (child_rows_with_null_fk) and leave at least one parent row without children; child rows are never dropped.
generic_sampling_rules.integer_numeric: Uniform integer within the range rule; include boundary values and one step on each side of listed literals.
generic_sampling_rules.text_short: Sample from a small pool of realistic literals; include near-variants (case change, trailing char, one-char substitution) of listed literals; allow NULL only if nullable.
generic_sampling_rules.text_long: Sample from a pool of question/description sentences; include near-variants of listed literals.
generic_sampling_rules.text_numeric_string: Sample numeric strings from a small pool; include boundary numeric literals as strings.
generic_sampling_rules.null_share: For nullable columns, plant exactly one NULL row per nullable column per instance (cap at 1 row, never a share of the table); the compact share is 0.0 observed, so keep NULLs rare but present; generated rows are never dropped, so the NULL is always planted; a planted NULL is never replaced to satisfy a rule.
generic_sampling_rules.fresh_value_share: About 10% of text values are fresh near-variants not in the literal pool.
generic_sampling_rules.size_distribution: Per-instance sizes are base +/- 30% (no geometric branch), capped at 230 and never below the original table size; the parent is filled before the child; the generated count must equal table_sizes_per_instance.
generic_sampling_rules.boundary_injection: Boundary and near-variant values are injected after formula enforcement; _apply_formulas must skip values already in the column's boundary target list so boundary values survive.
generic_sampling_rules.tie_forcing: Best-effort: samplers attempt to produce at least two groups with equal COUNT(*) at the listed ranks; tie separation is not guaranteed and is not a hard constraint.

issues.evidence: instance.py _apply_formulas only handles two formula shapes: 'col > N' and 'col BETWEEN N AND M'. The spec's semantic_rules_and_formulas are all of these two shapes, so this is fine for the current spec. However, _apply_formulas is called BEFORE _apply_null_rule, and _apply_null_rule can overwrite a value with NULL. The interface rule says 'a planted NULL is never replaced to satisfy a rule' — this is satisfied. But the reverse is not: _apply_formulas can replace a value that was a boundary value (e.g. Answer.UserID = 3) with a re-drawn value inside the rule's range, potentially destroying the comparison_boundary targets. The spec's Answer.UserID comparison_boundary targets values [3,4,5,6], and the formula 'UserID > 0' would not reject 3-6, so this is safe for UserID. But for Answer.SurveyID the formula 'SurveyID BETWEEN 2013 AND 2020' and the boundary targets [2013,2014,2015,2018,2019,2020] are compatible. No concrete violation observed, but the ordering is fragile.
